chunks: Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Hammad ibn Isa, from Ibrahim ibn Umar, from Abu Hamza al-Thumali, from Ali ibn al-Husayn (peace be upon him), who said:
Whoever clothes a believer, Allah will clothe him from the green garments.
And he said in another hadith: He will not cease to be in the guarantee of Allah as long as a fibre remains upon him.
ai.seo_question: What is the spiritual reward for clothing a believer according to Shia hadith?
ai.summary: In al-Kafi, this hadith from Imam Ali ibn al-Husayn (Zayn al-Abidin) establishes clothing a believer as a tangible act of charity (sadaqah) that guarantees divine protection and reward. The 'garments of green' (thiyab al-khudr) symbolize the eternal garments of Paradise, while the condition that the merit persists 'as long as a thread remains' emphasizes the enduring nature of this specific reward in Shia jurisprudence.
